issues: No way around the measurement found. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. The candidate cuts random multistart from 150 s to 100 s and adds 50 s of local search. That search starts from the best packing so far, applies a random symmetry, shifts one band of circles cyclically, then re-polishes and re-runs the LP. Total search time stays at about 150 s, well inside the 4-minute margin.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The harness still checks validity, and the radii are still shrunk by 1e-10 before returning. One small risk: if every multistart attempt in the first 100 s raised an exception, best would be None and best[0] would crash. This is very unlikely, and the run finished without a crash.
Both loops are timed with the clock, so results are not exactly repeatable even with the fixed seed. The incumbent has the same behaviour.

The numbers match the claim. Candidate -2.636 and incumbent -2.6360 are equal at the precision shown, so the difference is 0 and z = 0. There is one run on each side, so no real variance estimate is possible. Rejecting is consistent with no measured improvement.
